# Wed Nov 25 - Intro to Generalized linear models

Read [Ch 16](https://davidcschneider.github.io/StatisticalScience/LNotes/Pt5/Ch16.pdf) and [Ch 16.1](https://davidcschneider.github.io/StatisticalScience/LNotes/Pt5/Ch16_1.pdf) in Dr. Schneider's notes.

Let's write the 2-way ANOVA as a generalized linear model:

Distribution: \[H \sim N(\mu, \sigma)\]

Link function: \[H = \eta\]

Model: \[\eta = \beta_0 + \beta_{Alt}Alt + \beta_{Sp}SP + \beta_{Alt\cdot Sp}Alt\cdot Sp\]


```{r}
fly.data = read.csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ahurford/biol-4605-data/refs/heads/main/data/heteroz-alt-species.csv")
fly.data
```

```{r}
fly.model = glm(heterozygosity ~ species + elevation_km + species*elevation_km , family = gaussian(link = identity), data=fly.data)
anova(fly.model, test="Chisq") #Sequential deviances
require(car)
Anova(fly.model, type="III", test.statistic = "LR") #Adjusted deviances
deviance(fly.model)
```
